plain_english_policy: This bill mandates immediate revocation of teaching certificates and termination/cancellation of employment contracts for educators convicted of specific serious felonies involving children.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would require the State Superintendent of Education to automatically revoke certification and local school boards/employers to immediately cancel or terminate employment upon a conviction. The policy creates an exception to tenure laws (continuing service status) for these offenses, ensuring immediate removal from positions involving children.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors affirmatively advanced this bill to establish stricter standards for educator certification and employment following convictions of serious crimes against children.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would require the State Superintendent of Education to revoke the teaching or other educational certificate of any person convicted of a Class A felony or sex offense involving a child and would provide for the immediate cancellation of the employment contract..."

"(b) The State Superintendent of Education shall immediately revoke any certificate issued under this chapter when the holder is convicted of capital murder or any Class A felony, including, but not limited to, rape, murder, kidnapping, or robbery..."
§16-24-8.1: "Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, the employment contract of a teacher on continuing service status... shall be immediately cancelled"
